key_provisions_or_claims: Current smart robots cannot be granted legal personality given their level of autonomy
If robots attain full autonomy, perception and will, no obstacle to legal personality
Legal personality was proposed by the EU to fill the liability gap and protect victims
Opaque autonomous behaviour makes proving defect and attribution to manufacturer or user difficult
Examines Korea's Intelligent Robots Act and EU electronic person concept
named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
annotation.summary_en: Persian-language journal article assessing whether smart robots can be granted legal personality, based on the 2017 EU Parliament 'electronic person' resolution. It concludes that current robots' autonomy does not justify personhood, but that fully autonomous robots with perception and will could in future receive it.

annotation.title_en: Feasibility Study of Granting Legal Personality to Smart Robots Based on European Union Resolution (Electronic Person - 2017)
